question: How does Arjuna identify Krishna as the imperishable supreme principle?
premises: Arjuna calls Krishna the imperishable supreme to be known
Krishna is the supreme treasury of the universe
He protects sattvata dharma and is eternal person
inference: Arjuna identifies Krishna as the imperishable supreme principle and protector of dharma.
uncertainties: Long fused compounds analyzed as wholes
Printed commentary prose mixed with verse
plain_english: You are the imperishable supreme to be known; you are the supreme treasury of this universe; you are imperishable, protector of sattvata dharma, eternal person, in my thought. Thus the principle known by those whose dharma is continuous grasping and renunciation, transcending all paths, is protected; this very secret in this chapter has mostly been revealed by me in the goddess-hymn commentary, and by those of like heart with instruction it is understood by itself. What again, by clearer manifestation and speech?
